title: docs-platform/judge/v1 response
description: A provider's answer to one judge/v1 request. The verdict is a proposal; the core verifies the quote verbatim against the evidence it sent and discards a yes whose quote it cannot find.

verdict.description: For draft_edit: yes when a draft is returned, unknown otherwise.

quote.description: Required field: one evidence line copied verbatim when verdict is yes and require_quote is true; empty otherwise.

draft.description: draft_edit only: the proposed replacement text for the claim. Never applied automatically.

id.description: The model that actually answered (may differ from the requested one, e.g. after a server-side fallback).

cost_usd.description: List-price cost of this call; 0 for local models. For subscription-billed CLIs it is the CLI's own notional figure.

estimated.description: true when the numbers are an estimate (dry run, or the provider cannot report usage).

error.description: Set when no answer was produced; verdict is then unknown.

evidence.description: agentic mode: the evidence list. The core verifies every quote at path:line±2 (in the worktree, or at rev) and downgrades the verdict to unknown if any quote cannot be verified or a yes has none.

transcript.description: agentic mode: tool steps (arguments and result sizes only, never contents).

answer.description: (1.2) structured tasks (repo_drift, claim_facts, doc_facts): the model's answer object, passed through unchanged. The core validates it against the prompt's reply schema shape, re-checks every piece of evidence in it and derives the verdict; verdict stays unknown here.

answer_parse.description: (1.2) how answer was obtained: schema = the provider's schema-enforced structured output; fallback = found in free text by the tolerant parser; repaired = the tolerant parser removed stray closing braces; failed = no object (error.code is bad_reply). Parse failures are counted separately from other errors.
